title: sre-weekly-update-2026-07-18
content:
SRE Weekly Update — 2026-07-18

Owners / distribution:
- Owner: Priya Natarajan (SRE lead)
- On-call rotation this week: Ethan (primary), Maya (secondary), Liam (backup)
- Distribution: eng-sre, eng-platform, product-reliability

Summary highlights:
- Two notable incidents this week (summary + follow-ups).
- SLO status: overall steady but one customer-impacting latency SLO breach on 2026-07-15.
- On-call handoffs: improved checklist, still gaps in escalation docs.
- Action items: short-term mitigation for routing hot-paths; medium-term review of autoscaling policies.

Incidents:
1) Incident: "tokenization-service latency spike" — 2026-07-15 02:10–02:55 UTC
   - Impact: elevated p99 latency on tokenization service affecting hosted API text-generation requests (~6% of traffic). Some customer requests timed out after 10s leading to retries and increased load on downstream runtime.
   - Detection: automated latency SLO alert fired at 02:15 UTC; paging to on-call.
   - Root cause (initial): a sudden increase in short-sequence chat traffic caused contention in the service thread pool combined with a recent change to request header parsing (rollout 2026-07-14).
   - Mitigation: rolled back the header parsing change at 02:30 UTC; increased tokenization pool size temporarily; enabled a rate-limit on internal retry loops to prevent thundering herd. Full client-facing SLO returned to normal by 02:55 UTC.
   - Post-incident actions: revert validated in staging; create a canary for header parsing change (JIRA-SRE-789). Add a circuit-breaker on inter-service retries. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-07-25.

2) Incident: "redis-cluster partial outage" — 2026-07-16 11:45–12:40 UTC
   - Impact: KV cache misses rose, increasing token generation tail latency for dedicated and private deployments in us-west-2; affected two enterprise customers with high qps.
   - Detection: monitoring alert for redis replication lag + increased cache miss rate.
   - Root cause: transient network partition between two AZs in us-west-2 combined with an aggressive failover timeout; redis replica took longer to promote.
   - Mitigation: manually promoted a healthy replica, temporarily increased cache TTLs to reduce load on redis, and routed heavy traffic to a read-replica pool in another region for affected enterprise customers. Service recovered by 12:40 UTC.
   - Post-incident actions: update runbook to include cross-AZ failover checklist; tune failover timeout in the redis operator. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-07-30.

SLOs and reliability metrics:
- Production request success SLO (5xx rate) — target 99.95% monthly: current month-to-date 99.97%. No action.
- Latency SLO (hosted API p99 text generation) — target 750ms p99: week average 680ms but spike on 2026-07-15 caused 1-day breach (breach window captured in incident 1).
- Cache hit rate SLO (tokenization KV cache) — target 92%: current 90.8% (down due to redis incident).
- Availability for dedicated pools — target 99.9%: met.

Notes and observations:
- Increased short-chat traffic patterns observed after the marketing campaign from 2026-07-14; workload characterization shows more concurrent short-lived sessions which stress thread pools differently than long streaming sessions. Need to update capacity planning to include these workload shapes.
- Recent deployment (header parsing) passed unit/integration tests but lacked a staged canary — primary lesson: any change in hot-path request-parsing must be canaried with low-latency traffic shape.
- On-call rotation handled pages well; the main time-to-detect was quick but resolution required code rollback. Continue to emphasize safe rollouts and rollback playbooks.

On-call handoffs / runbook updates:
- Handoff notes (Ethan -> Maya on 2026-07-17 08:00 UTC): open incidents reviewed; Ethan left a checklist of escalation steps for tokenization-service and link to debugging dashboards (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Updated runbooks this week: added explicit steps for redis partial partitions and a quick rollback playbook for tokenization header parsing.
- Gaps identified: escalation contacts for enterprise customer support (CS) for private deployments are out-of-date. Action: update contact list and include CS-runbooks. Owner: Liam. Due: 2026-07-22.

Operational work / upcoming changes:
- Autoscaling policy review: product and infra to meet 2026-07-22 to propose conservative scale-up thresholds for the short-chat traffic pattern. Owner: Priya + infra team.
- Canary plan for request header parsing change (safe rollout): design canary (1% low-latency traffic) + observability checks before increasing to 10%. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-07-21.
- Redis operator tuning: slack thread started; plan to experiment on staging next week. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-07-30.
- Instrumentation: add more fine-grained tracing for tokenization hot-paths (span timing for parse -> tokenize -> cache lookup). Owner: Eng Observability. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/456.

Meeting notes (SRE weekly sync 2026-07-17):
- Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Maya, Liam, product-reliability rep (Hannah), infra eng (Rahul).
- Agenda: incident reviews, SLO trends, canary policies, on-call hiring coverage.
- Decisions:
  - Add canary requirement for any request-parsing change that touches hosted API path. (Action: Ethan to draft canary template)
  - Prioritize autoscaling policy changes for tokenization pool as high-priority (Action: Priya to coordinate with infra).
  - Update customer escalation contacts and include in runbooks (Action: Liam).
- Parking lot: revisit circuit-breaker tuning vs retry heuristics in August.

Action items (summary):
- Ethan: create canary template + implement 1% canary for header parsing changes. Due 2026-07-21.
- Maya: update redis runbook and tune failover timeout on operator. Due 2026-07-30.
- Liam: update enterprise CS contacts in runbooks and publish. Due 2026-07-22.
- Priya + infra: autoscaling thresholds proposal. Due 2026-07-22.
- Eng Observability: add trace spans for tokenization path. Due 2026-07-29.

Risks / blockers:
- Short-chat traffic growth might increase frequency of tail-latency events; need proactive capacity planning and better synthetic traffic tests.
- Lack of a standardized canary template slows safe rollouts.

Misc notes / personal TODOs:
- Follow up with product on campaign-related traffic forecasts.
- Schedule a 30-min runbook walk-through for new SRE hires next week.

Attachments / dashboards referenced:
- Latency dashboard: CONFLUENCE-1234 (linked)
- Redis cluster metrics: grafana:dashboards/redis-us-west-2
- Incident timelines: JIRA-SRE-789

End of update.
